title: I never knew what You did
hookLine: I didn't recognize what You did; You made me worthy (Mundavani salok M5, ang 1429)

cards: Years later, you find out. The neighbor who quietly paid a bill when your family was struggling. The teacher who argued for you in a meeting you never knew happened.
The parent who skipped something they wanted so you could have what you needed. You lived through those years thinking you'd managed on your own.
Then the curtain lifts, and you see the hands that were holding things up the whole time. A short salok near the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib is about exactly that moment.

teach.h: A SALOK AT THE VERY END.
teach.b: The salok is by Guru Arjan, on Ang fourteen twenty-nine, right after the Mundavani, the seal he set on the Granth. Its first words are teraa keetaa jaato naahee.
In paraphrase: I did not recognize what You did for me; You made me worthy. I am unworthy, with no virtue of my own, and You took pity on me. You had mercy, and I met the true Guru, my friend.
Nanak says, if I receive the Name, I live, and my body and mind bloom. Look at the order.

teach.h: I DIDN'T NOTICE WHAT YOU DID.
teach.b: First, a confession: I didn't notice.
Then the surprise: You made me worthy anyway. The word for worthy is jog. It sounds like yoga, but here it simply means fit, capable, deserving.
The worthiness wasn't earned and then rewarded. It was given, and only seen afterward. Where the salok sits matters too.
It's among the last words before the Raagmala, the index of raags at the very end.

teach.h: THANKS AT THE CLOSE OF A READING.
teach.b: When a family or a gurdwara completes a full reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, at a bhog, this salok is read near the close.
So after more than fourteen hundred pages, the reading ends not with an achievement but with thanks: You did it, and I didn't even know.
The same turn can come at the end of any long effort, a degree, a recovery, a hard year: you look back and see the help you missed.

how: This salok of Guru Arjan is read near the close of a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, at the bhog, just before the Raagmala.

o: a reward for good deeds done
a yoga pose held for stillness
fit, made worthy, as a gift

games.q: you've just finished reading all of the Guru Granth Sahib with your family. what kind of words come near the very end?
o: a list of what you achieved.
thanks: I didn't recognize what You did, and You made me worthy.
a warning about the next reading.
games.why: Guru Arjan's salok ends the long reading with gratitude for help unseen, not with an achievement.

practice: Let your mind go back to one stretch of your life you think you got through alone, and look again: who drove, cooked, covered for you, prayed for you, paid for something? Let one face come, hold it, and say a silent thank you.
If you pray, say Waheguru for the help you still haven't seen.

wordCard.voice: Jog, fit, worthy: Guru Arjan's salok near the end of the Granth says I didn't recognize what You did for me; unworthy as I was, You made me so.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: fit, worthy; in this salok, 'You made me worthy'.

carryVoice: Your line: you made me worthy. The help was there long before you saw it. See you tomorrow.
